goal: Score reviewer configurations against the eval corpus with an offline runner, record the baseline of the current single-reviewer pipeline, publish a record-based review-quality report, and add session-visible quality metrics to the imm-retro analyzer within its existing counting rules and boundary.

acceptance.assertion: Meet S1 in docs/specs/review-verifier-eval.spec.md: the runner scores a reviewer configuration per gold case (recall over confirmed_true by anchor match or by violated.ref plus first caller_chain path matching the gold location, false positives as blocking findings on clean cases plus matches to confirmed_false anchors, unknown anchors reported separately as new-anchor rate, and no recall or precision denominator ever includes unlabeled cases); a baseline run for the current pipeline is committed under benchmark-results/review-eval and its numbers are recorded in the corpus README; the record-based report computes, from committed audit records only and never live .imm state, rounds-to-pass median and p95, the resolved / refuted / accepted_risk disposition mix, the security_boundary share of blocking findings, and advisory count per pass; the imm-retro analyzer additionally reports per author model the blocking split by violated.kind and refute / resolve / accept-residual-risk event counts only where a committed fixture proves the source event is visible in session logs, and a fixture without violated.kind yields the pre-change report unchanged; the merge gate is written down with it: recall not lower, clean-case false-positive rate not higher, rounds-to-pass p95 not higher, and recall wins any trade-off. It also carries the S1 Jev supplement (spec item 6): a security_boundary mislabel rate from an offline classification of each blocking finding's violated.kind, reported beside the raw share as experimental until scored against the S0 gold cases, never changing a finding, record, or admission. It also carries a per-acceptance repeat-count series (spec item 7, the data half of #204 S1): per acceptance ID, its rework-finding count across rounds and rounds since its last finding, from committed records only; it decides nothing by itself.
